results.reply: "Evenin' to ye. I'm Padraig Darcy—this damp patch of floorboards has been mine these thirty years. What'll ye have, stranger, or are ye just after shelterin' from the fine weather?"
"Ah, Seamus Ó Conchúir, you soggy-looking creature—come in out of that drizzle before you melt entirely. I'll not have you tracking half the parish's mud across Brigid's floor."
"Ah, Seamus Ó Briain, you old rogue—come in out of that mist before you take your death, and tell me what keeps a decent man from his dinner this hour."
"Evenin' to ye. I'm Brigid O'Brien, the midwife hereabouts—if it's herbs or healing ye need, or if yer wife's time is comin', ye'll find me in the village."
"Siobhán, is that you? Come in out of the wet—I've the kettle on and a poultice to mix before Mrs. Flaherty's time comes."
"Father Cullen. The mist has you looking like a ghost yourself—come, I've boiled the kettle and there's yarrow for that cough I heard last month."

"Good evening to you. I am Father Cathal Donnellan, and I serve the parish of Saint Colman's—though I confess I find myself in this establishment more often than my superiors might wish, seeking souls who stray from the path."
"Good morrow to ye, Siobhán. I see the rain has not kept ye from the old woman's door—though I wonder what business brings ye here once more."
"Mist, ye come again to the Lord's threshold though the old paths yet cling to yer step. Enter, then, and let the true Word find ye whilst the bell still tolls."
"Evenin'. Sean Murphy's the name, though most here just call me the bogman when they need peat for their fires. You'll not find a drier sod in three counties."
